Commentary.Commentary: Australia, on the other hand, will be happy with the way they bounced back into the game. Faulkner was the pick of the bowlers as his change of pace made life difficult for the batsmen taking 3/59. Starc came in well for his last spell to rattle off the tail-enders. The pitch seems a good one to bat if the batsmen apply themselves for sometime in the middle. It won't be an easy chase for the young Australian side who are looking to make it even in this series. Join us in a while for the chase.

A mediocre batting performance by the Kiwis after managing to stay on top of the game for more than half of their innings. After being 162/2 at the 30-over mark, the Kiwis only managed to rack up another 119 runs in the last 20 overs losing 8 wickets in the process. Ross Taylor was brilliant with the bat as he added another ton to his name. Brownlie got his maiden fifty but departed soon after. That triggered a collapse as the hosts went from 176 for 2 to 209 for 6 in no time. Taylor didn't last long after his ton and it was down to the lower order to get them to a good score. Santner began really slowly but picked up pace towards the end, scoring a 34-ball 38. None of the other batsmen though could use the platform for their very own benefit to make this a par total.
OUT b Mitchell Starc. New Zealand have lost their ninth wicket.
OUT b Mitchell Starc. New Zealand have lost their eighth wicket.
OUT c Marcus Stoinis b James Faulkner. New Zealand have lost their seventh wicket.

UPDATE AT 45 OVERS, NZ 229/6 - The Kiwis have neither lost a single wicket nor managed to score a bucket of runs - just 21 in the last five overs. They will have to go berserk as they only have 5 overs left. The Aussies have been quite disciplined with their line and lengths as they have hardly bowled a bad delivery. Can the Black Caps end on a high note?
OUT b Josh Hazlewood. New Zealand have lost their sixth wicket.

UPDATE AT 40 OVERS, NZ 208/5 - Just what the doctor ordered for the visitors there. The hosts have only managed to rack up another 15 runs with the loss of a couple of wickets. Munro and Broom could not trouble the scorers as they both headed back early. Neesham and Taylor would hope to stay till the end so that they can post a challenging total somewhere around 300. The latter has hardly got any strike but the home side will want to change that if they want to trouble the opposition. Can the away side keep the charge on with the ball?
OUT c Mitchell Starc b Josh Hazlewood. New Zealand have lost their fifth wicket.
OUT c Peter Handscomb b James Faulkner. New Zealand have lost their fourth wicket.

UPDATE AT 35 OVERS, NZ 193/3 - Faulkner finally got a breakthrough as he sent Brownlie back into the hut with a slower one. The Kiwis have still managed to score 31 runs in the last five overs and will be thinking of posting a total of more than 300. Broom and Taylor are nudging around for runs for now but it looks like the big shots may be round the corner. The visitors will want to pick wickets as soon as possible to put some pressure on the hosts.
OUT c Peter Handscomb b James Faulkner. New Zealand have lost their third wicket.

UPDATE AT 30 OVERS, NZ 162/2 - Brownlie and Taylor both have managed to get to their respective fifties. They look settled out in the middle and will hope to continue in the same manner and get big scores under their belt. Finch called his main man Starc back into the attack but even he could not cause any damage. These two batsmen out in the middle are giving Finch a tough time. Can the visitors bounce back in the game with a couple of quick wickets?

UPDATE AT 25 OVERS, NZ 133/2 - Taylor is looking sublime with the bat as he is punishing all the bad deliveries and also making some good balls look bad. Runs have dried up for Brownlie as he hasn't managed to score a single boundary since the 10th over. Faulkner and Stoinis have managed to keep the score in check but have never looked intimidating. Ross Taylor might just be the difference between the two sides if he keeps going.

UPDATE AT 20 OVERS, NZ 106/2 - Taylor and Brownlie are keeping the scoreboard ticking as they are playing shots all round the ground. The latter is closing onto his maiden ODI fifty. Both these batsmen will want to stay in the middle as long as possible and set a platform for the upcoming batsmen to launch. The Australian bowlers haven't looked that effective throughout the passage of play. They will want to get a wicket out of somewhere before it gets too late for them.

UPDATE AT 15 OVERS, NZ 76/2 - Just when it was looking like a quiet passage of play, a Cummins delivery just came up by surprise which totally outdid the Kiwi skipper Williamson. He was looking solid in the middle and would be really disappointed to get out after settling in. Can the visitors get a couple of more wickets now to put the pressure back on the hosts?
OUT c Peter Handscomb b Pat Cummins. New Zealand have lost their second wicket.

UPDATE AT 10 OVERS, NZ 59/1 - Williamson has taken the charge to the opposition. Just when it seemed like Brownlie was playing a silent knock, he came up with a couple of beautiful looking boundaries off Cummins. The Kiwis would look to build up on these previous six overs as they look to set a big total. Australia, on the other hand, will need to pick up wickets at regular intervals to get back on top?

UPDATE AT 5 OVERS, NZ 18/1 - Sensational start for the Aussies! They missed out on an LBW review against Latham off Starc in the very first over. It surely looked plumb to the naked eye but they did not go for it. Starc, however, got his man in his very next over. Williamson and Brownlie have steadied the ship since then and have also managed to put some runs on the board. There is some movement for the pacers but the ball is coming nicely onto the bat which makes it a good batting track for now.
OUT c Josh Hazlewood b Mitchell Starc. New Zealand have lost their first wicket.
Australia XI - Aaron Finch(c), Shaun Marsh, Travis Head, Peter Handscomb(w), Glenn Maxwell, Marcus Stoinis, James Faulkner, Pat Cummins, Mitchell Starc, Adam Zampa, Josh Hazlewood.
New Zealand XI - Dean Brownlie, Tom Latham(w), Kane Williamson(c), Ross Taylor, Neil Broom, Colin Munro, James Neesham, Mitchell Santner, Tim Southee, Lockie Ferguson, Trent Boult.
TOSS - New Zealand win the toss and elect to bat first.

The visiting team have quite a few players who are eyeing to cement their spots for the upcoming Champions Trophy 2017. The hosts will be missing the services of Martin Guptill who has been ruled out due to an injury. Adam Zampa and Ish Sodhi might be given a look in their respective teams as the pitch in Hamilton might assist spin. It should be a cracker of a match. Join us in a while for the toss. Due to lack of television feed, there won't be ball-by-ball commentary for this match but we shall keep you posted with updates after every five overs.

Welcome for the final ODI between New Zealand and Australia of the Chappell-Hadlee Trophy 2017. It should be an exciting contest as both the teams have a lot at stake. New Zealand will regain the trophy if they win today. While, Australia will take it back home if they emerge victorious as they are the current holders of the trophy. The win will also safeguard their No.1 ranking in ODI cricket.
